sources.title: Keeping records for Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)
Prepare for the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)

facts.source_fact: Importers must retain records for CBAM goods they believe are exempt.
Published exemption categories include private use.
Published exemption categories include UK-origin goods.
Published exemption categories include Returned Goods Relief.
Published exemption categories include temporary admission with full relief from customs duty.
Private-use evidence can include proof of ownership and how the goods are used privately.
UK-origin evidence can include production records, invoices, accounting details and supplier declarations.
Returned Goods Relief records can include prior export, reimport within three years and evidence the goods are in the same state.
Temporary-admission records include evidence of eligibility, the import declaration showing full relief and compliance with admission terms.
Belief that goods are exempt does not remove the duty to keep evidence supporting the exemption.
